kitDescription: Bready is a Water SR Burst-III attacker whose kit splits in half depending on what kind of buff her team feeds her. An ally buff that raises sustained damage puts her into Lingering Taste; a distributed-damage buff (received while she has no sustained-damage buff) puts her into Recommended Taste instead, and each taste cancels the other. Either taste costs her 20% Charge Speed for 50 seconds, so she charges more slowly whichever branch she is on. In Lingering Taste every third full-charge hit makes the boss take 10.2% more damage for 5 seconds and applies Aftertaste, a 150.04%-of-ATK sustained tick every second for 5 seconds, and her burst amplifies that Aftertaste effect by 349.8%. In Recommended Taste each full-charge hit instead grants her 60.01% Attack Damage for 5 seconds and fires a 265.07% distributed hit at all enemies, and her burst grants 70.09% ATK. Regardless of taste she gains 70.01% ATK whenever the team enters Full Burst, plus 60.19% Attack Damage for 10 seconds from her own burst cast.

redAssertions: Taste exclusivity: 'modes length === 2' — driver ships 3 modes [auto,sustained,distributed]; blind assumed a 2-element taste pair. MODE-ARITY, not a kit divergence.

S1b/c: 'a chargeSpeedPct -20 self buffApply exists' + 'sign-flipping to +20 raises damage' — driver models the ▼20% as charFixes.chargeFrames 72 (no buffApply event). Driver is engine-correct: chargeSpeedPct is clamped to >=0 before `needed = chargeFrames × (1 − cs/100)`, so a −20 buff is INERT (the blind's encoding is a 'modeled ≠ working' drop). RECON_ERROR by the blind.

S2a Damage Taken 10.2 present / team lift / drop-counterfactual (3 asserts) — blind's reverseModes() on a 3-element array selected 'distributed', never 'sustained', so the Lingering branch was never exercised. MODE-SELECTION artifact.
S2a Aftertaste dot structural + drop-counterfactual — same mode-selection artifact (dot lives in the sustained-mode block).
S2a '1-per-3-charges vs 1-per-charge ratio' — same artifact (Lingering branch never live).
S2b/c Recommended rider asserts — blind's 'recommended' run resolved to default `auto` (tasteless), so attackDamagePct 60.01 and the 265.07 rider read 0. MODE-SELECTION artifact.
Bb 'Aftertaste Effect 349.8 present + inertness pair' — same artifact.
Bc 'atkPct 70.09 present in Recommended' — same artifact.
'exactly one Taste branch live per run and flipping swaps it' — same artifact.

NOTE: all 11 REDs root-cause to exactly two things — the 2-mode-vs-3-mode arity/selection mismatch and the charge-speed MECHANISM (where the driver is provably right). ZERO reds attribute to a magnitude, trigger identity, target set, scope, duration or flavor disagreement. The blind S6 override independently reproduces all 10 lines with identical magnitudes/triggers/targets/durations/flavors, so the two families CONVERGE on the encoding; the mechanical GREEN is only partial (7 asserts) and the blind suite never reached the sustained branch.

gotchas.summary: The shipped default mode is `auto` (tasteless), but the override's own note AND caveat both state the default is `sustained` — the artifact contradicts its own documentation, and the default the board actually runs leaves 6 of 10 kit lines inert while still paying the charge-speed penalty.
gotchas.evidence: Shipped: "modes": ["auto","sustained","distributed"] (first = default). Note: "modeled as user-selectable `modes` [sustained, distributed] … DEFAULT sustained (her signature Aftertaste sustained-DoT identity + the burst's biggest line 349.8% is Lingering-gated)". Caveat 1: "(default: sustained = Lingering Taste …)". Driver test H10 asserts the opposite and calls it deliberate: "the default `auto` mode (= tasteless) leaves EVERY taste-gated line inert". Blind S6 defaulted to lingeringTaste and separately flagged the no-taste state as a real third state worth adding. Consequence per §1e/§1g: in `auto` her whole skill2 (boss Damage Taken 10.2 team amp, Aftertaste dot, the 60.01 Attack Damage self buff, the 265.07 distributed rider) and burst lines 2–3 contribute nothing, while charFixes.chargeFrames 72 still costs her shots — a strictly net-negative default.
gotchas.suggestedFix: Reconcile before merge — this is a one-line pick, not a magnitude: either (a) ship ["sustained","auto","distributed"] to match the note's stated default and rationale, or (b) keep `auto` first and rewrite the note + caveat to say the default is tasteless and WHY (i.e. no scope-lock teammate grants a sustained- or distributed-damage buff, so the literal prose leaves her tasteless). If (b), also state that the unconditional charge penalty makes `auto` pessimistic and that the taste-carrying modes are the ones to use for any comp containing a sustained/distributed buffer.

gotchas.summary: 'Aftertaste Effect ▲ 349.8%' is encoded as an ADDITIVE sustainedDamagePct term in the shared Damage-Up bucket rather than as a multiplier on the named Aftertaste effect — the downstream effect is modeled, not the named mechanic, and the two readings differ by ~41% on her tick values.
gotchas.evidence: Kit: "Aftertaste Effect ▲ 349.8% for 10 sec" (Lingering-gated, self). §1e places Sustained Damage ▲ additively inside DamageUp, so 349.8 is DILUTED by her own 60.19 attackDamagePct and by any team Damage-Up; a named-effect multiplier would scale the 150.04% tick directly (≈674.9%) and be undiluted. Driver quantified it (×5.10 additive vs ×7.20 multiplicative); blind S6 independently chose the same additive encoding and raised the same scope-widening caveat; S2b pre-flagged it as a ⚑ the driver must state rather than silently pick.
gotchas.suggestedFix: Leave as-is (additive) and keep the ⚑ — do NOT pick a number to move the board. Measurement recipe: a bready-focus recording in a Lingering team; read one Aftertaste tick popup immediately BEFORE her burst and one INSIDE her 10s window, remove the known FB/crit/core/element factors, and compare the ratio against the two predictions (additive ≈ ×5.10 with this fixture's Damage-Up present, multiplicative ≈ ×7.20 independent of other Damage-Up). Additionally add a cheap sim-side isolation now — drop the dot and the 349.8 buff together and confirm the totals are identical to dropping the dot alone — to prove the buff routes onto the dot at all.

gotchas.summary: The Aftertaste/Damage-Taken proc rate rides on hitCount:3 and NOTHING in the driver's suite pins the ~1-per-3-full-charges cadence, so a count-inflating hitCount (if it also counts Aftertaste dot ticks or the rider) or a count:1 encoding would both pass green. UNVERIFIED BY THIS JUDGE — no code read available.
gotchas.evidence: Kit: "Activates after landing 3 Full Charge attack(s)". Driver encodes {kind:"hitCount", count:3} and asserts only presence + the 5s duration + mode inertness; the DoT test asserts the modal 60f tick gap, not the instance count. If hitCount counts every damage instance by her rather than weapon hits, each 5-tick Aftertaste instance feeds the next proc and the debuff/DoT uptime becomes self-reinforcing — a classic 'modeled ≠ working' inflation. S2b's distinguishing assertion and the blind's ratio test (Recommended per-shot count between 2× and 4.5× the Lingering proc count) are exactly the pins that would catch it; the blind's version never executed because its mode selection never reached the sustained branch.
gotchas.suggestedFix: Add one assertion to the sustained run: count(bossDebuff damageTakenPct 10.2) ≈ floor(breadyShots / 3) within a reload-gap tolerance, and count(Aftertaste ticks) ≈ 5 × that proc count. Confirm by inspection which instances the engine's hitCount trigger increments (weapon hits only vs all damage events); if it counts dot ticks or the distributed rider, switch to a full-charge/shot-scoped counter. No magnitude change either way.

gotchas.summary: charFixes.chargeFrames 72 is unconditional, so the Taste-only Charge Speed ▼20% is also paid in the tasteless `auto` state where the prose grants no taste and therefore no penalty.
gotchas.evidence: Kit: the ▼20% exists only as "Lingering Taste:" / "Recommended Taste:" payloads. Driver caveat: "the Taste Charge Speed ▼20% debuff is modeled as a permanent charge-time increase (60→72 frames; assumes she is always in a taste)", and the test header repeats it. §4 confirms charge time is the only expressible channel (chargeSpeedPct clamps at 0, so the blind's −20 buff would be inert). Interacts with gotcha 1: with `auto` as the shipped default this documented gap becomes the live board configuration.
gotchas.suggestedFix: Keep the encoding (it is the only channel that works) and keep the caveat. If the mode-conditional form is ever wanted, it needs a mode-gated charge-time primitive; until then, resolving gotcha 1 in favour of a taste-carrying default makes the unconditional penalty correct by construction rather than merely documented.

verdictRationale: All 10 kit lines are FAITHFUL (8) or DOCUMENTED_GAP (2) — every magnitude, bucket, trigger identity, target set, duration and flavor matches the prose and the formula SSOT, and the two cross-family blind re-derivations CONVERGE on all of them (the S2b spec and the S6 override reproduce the same 10 encodings independently). The S5 mechanical run is RED (7 pass / 11 fail / 4 skip) but ZERO failures are faithfulness divergences: nine are artifacts of the blind assuming a 2-element taste pair, so its reverseModes() selected `distributed` and then `auto` and never exercised the sustained branch at all; the other two are the charge-speed MECHANISM, where the driver is provably right (chargeSpeedPct clamps to >=0, so the blind's −20 buff would be silently inert and only a longer chargeFrames can slow an SR — a genuine 'modeled ≠ working' catch by the driver, and a RECON_ERROR by the blind, as is its claim that enemy-targeted damage resolves to []). Ranked real findings: (1) the shipped default mode `auto` contradicts the override's own note and caveat, which both say `sustained` — undocumented, board-visible, and it makes 6 of 10 lines inert while still charging her the charge-speed penalty; fix the array or fix the note before merge, it is a one-line pick with no magnitude content. (2) The 349.8% 'Aftertaste Effect' additive-vs-multiplicative reading (~41% on her tick values) — properly ⚑-flagged, measurement-gated, out of scope to decide here. (3) hitCount:3 has no cadence assertion, so the Aftertaste/Damage-Taken proc rate is unpinned and a count-inflating or count:1 model would pass green — this is why discriminationOk is false; the rest of the load-bearing set does discriminate (H1/H7 pin FB-enter vs burstCast by exact frame in both directions, H2's 72→60 counterfactual proves the charge debuff gates shot count, every taste-gated line is asserted inert in the opposite mode, and the rider's crit/no-core/no-range triple is pinned). Neither undocumented item is a wrong mechanic, so this is a GO conditional on those two cheap additions, not a faithfulness rejection. Same-model residual for the owner to spot-check: the sustained (Lingering) branch was verified ONLY by the driver's own suite — the independent blind never reached it — so the boss Damage-Taken debuff, the Aftertaste dot cadence, and the 349.8 buff actually landing on the tick values all rest on a single family's assertions; the fastest independent check is the sustained run's proc-count ratio plus the drop-dot/drop-boost inertness pair.
